official.deadline_note: The merit (performance) scholarship window runs 21 September - 30 October 2026 for the 2025/26 academic year. The separate faculty funding scholarship for thesis costs has its own windows - e.g. Humanities 20 April - 29 May 2026 and 14 September - 23 October 2026; URBI 20 April - 21 May 2026 and 14 September - 23 October 2026. Applications always go to your own faculty, never to a central scholarships office.
official.application_cycle: academic year 2025/26 (assessment period 1 October 2025 - 30 September 2026); call published in the University Gazette issue of 15 April 2026
official.status_note: The 2025/26 call is currently running: applications for the merit scholarship are submitted via the 'Merit Scholarship' app in UNIGRAZonline from 21 September to 30 October 2026.
official.tuition_coverage_note: No University of Graz scholarship page states any tuition-fee coverage, so the cash award sits on top of fees. Fees are charged separately: EU/EEA students pay EUR 25.20 per semester for the minimum duration of study plus a tolerance semester and EUR 363.36 thereafter; third-country degree students pay EUR 726.72 per semester plus the student union (OeH) fee, unless an exemption or equal status applies.
benefits: A performance scholarship may be awarded in an amount no less than EUR 750 and no more than EUR 1,500 - a one-off payment per academic year
A separate funding scholarship is a one-time award of EUR 750 to EUR 3,600 for master's-thesis or dissertation costs (stays abroad, conference fees, extensive literature search, empirical studies)
Awarding of a performance scholarship does not depend on the socio-economic situation of the applicant
There is no legal entitlement to a performance scholarship; it is awarded by the dean of studies within the framework of private administration
Students from the poorest countries listed in the appendix of the Tuition Fee Regulation pay only the OeH student union fee each semester
eligibility: Austrian citizens, EEA citizens as well as stateless persons and refugees as defined in Section 4 of the Student Support Act (StudFG)
Enrolled in a regular (ordinary) degree programme at the University of Graz (Karl-Franzens-Universitaet Graz)
Outstanding academic results achieved in accordance with the study regulations of the degree programme
Compliance with the entitlement period - the legally stipulated study time plus one additional semester (Sections 18, 19 StudFG)
Consistently good academic practice, in particular no use of unauthorised aids in examinations or written work
requirements: Bachelor's, Master's and teacher training: at least 60 positively completed ECTS credit points in the academic year, of which at least 50 must be positively graded (10 may be assessed as 'successfully participated')
A weighted grade point average of the study achievements used for assessment may not exceed 2.0 (of the best 50 courses with the highest grades and most ECTS credit points)
SOWI Faculty: at least 48 positively completed ECTS points in the assessment period, with a grade point average no worse than 2.0
Doctoral candidates: completion of the doctorate within the assessment period, dissertation graded 'excellent' and doctoral examination 'passed with distinction' (Humanities)
Proof of any study delays as defined in Sections 18 and 19 StudFG, where the entitlement period is exceeded
documents: Certificate of registration for the place of residence (Meldebestaetigung)
For non-Austrian citizens: proof of belonging to the eligible group of persons (e.g. permanent residence card)
Recognition notifications, plus the underlying certificate where no grade or semester hours are listed, for anything not visible in UNIGRAZonline
Transcripts and study achievement certificates for examinations that do not show up in UNIGRAZonline, including certificates from other universities
selection_criteria: If the number of qualifying applications exceeds the number of scholarships, applications are ranked by the grade point average of the 50 highest-graded, most ECTS courses
Ties are then broken by the number of additional positively completed ECTS credit points (including courses assessed as 'successfully participated')
The same parameters can also be taken into account in the amount that is awarded
Awarding is done by the dean of studies; there is no legal entitlement to an award
Faculty-specific criteria are published each year in the University Gazette (Mitteilungsblatt)
coverage: One-off cash award of EUR 750 to EUR 1,500 per academic year (performance / merit scholarship)

Funding scholarship, one-off EUR 750 to EUR 3,600: domestic and/or international thesis-related travel, participation in conferences and congresses, extensive literature search, empirical studies, and printing costs for publication up to a maximum of EUR 400

Not covered: tuition fees, living costs, laptops and other multi-year equipment, books available in sufficient quantity in a Graz library, flat-rate accommodation costs, catering expenses, office supplies, binding and reproduction costs for theses
application_method: Electronically via the 'Merit Scholarship' / 'My Performance Studentship' app in UNIGRAZonline; the app is only displayed during the application period
If electronic submission is not possible (e.g. no active student account), contact the dean's office by e-mail with the required documents, or use the faculty application form (SOWI) sent by e-mail
An application may only be submitted to one faculty - the one where most ECTS credit points were earned; a scholarship is only granted for one degree programme
Funding scholarship applications are e-mailed to the dean's office with the application form, cost statement, content description (expose) and at least one expert opinion attached
official.application_route: Apply online through the 'Merit Scholarship' app in UNIGRAZonline between 21 September and 30 October 2026, submitting to the single faculty where you earned the most ECTS.
official.study_mode: full-time, enrolled in an ordinary degree programme (as published: 'ordentliches Studium')
official.citizenship_residency: Austrian citizens, EEA citizens, stateless persons and refugees as defined in Section 4 StudFG may apply. Third-country nationals are not an eligible group unless they hold equal-status documentation (e.g. permanent residence card).
official.international_eligibility: Yes for EEA citizens and for stateless persons and refugees with equal status; no for third-country nationals without equal-status documentation.
official.research_requirement: For the funding scholarship only: an announced but not yet completed master's thesis or dissertation, a description of the content of the planned work (expose), and at least one expert opinion - normally from the thesis supervisor - on the cost breakdown.
official.duration: assessment period 1 October 2025 to 30 September 2026 (academic year 2025/26); the award itself is a one-off payment
official.description: The University of Graz awards merit-based performance scholarships of EUR 750-1,500 to enrolled students with outstanding academic results, together with one-off funding scholarships of EUR 750-3,600 for thesis-related costs. Awards are decided by each faculty's dean of studies under the Austrian Student Support Act and carry no legal entitlement.
official.program_type: Merit (performance) scholarship and funding scholarship - university-internal awards

applicant_utility.summary: This is not an award you can win before you enrol - only students already enrolled in an ordinary degree programme at the University of Graz may apply, and only Austrian, EEA, stateless or refugee applicants with equal status qualify, so a third-country national studying in Graz cannot receive it. The real window is 21 September to 30 October 2026 for the 2025/26 academic year, applied for through a 'Merit Scholarship' app that appears in UNIGRAZonline only during those six weeks. Treat the EUR 750-1,500 as a single payment that sits on top of your semester fees rather than as a funding package that replaces them.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Already-enrolled EEA or equal-status students at Graz with a heavy, well-graded transcript and a GPA close to 2.0 or better.
application_readiness_checklist: Before the window opens, check that your ECTS count for the assessment period (1 Oct 2025 - 30 Sep 2026) clears the faculty threshold - 60 ECTS with at least 50 graded at Humanities/URBI, 48 ECTS at SOWI - and compute your weighted GPA over your best 50 courses.
Confirm you are still inside the entitlement period (standard study time plus one tolerance semester); being a semester over without a documented reason is fatal.
Make sure your Meldebestaetigung (residence registration) is current and that your bank details are already entered in UNIGRAZonline before you start.
If you are not an Austrian citizen, obtain proof of belonging to the eligible group of persons (e.g. permanent residence card) in advance - a passport alone will not do.
Log in during the window and verify the 'Merit Scholarship' app actually appears in UNIGRAZonline, because it disappears again after 30 October.
Apply to only one faculty - the one where you earned the most ECTS - and remember one scholarship per study year.
common_rejection_risks: Applying to the wrong faculty while enrolled in more than one programme; only one application is permitted and only one award per study year is granted.
Missing the six-week app window entirely because the merit-scholarship application only appears in UNIGRAZonline between 21 September and 30 October.
A GPA above 2.0 on the courses actually counted, or fewer ECTS than the faculty threshold in the assessment year - the requirements are strict and faculty-set.
Incomplete submissions: SOWI states plainly that missing documents are not chased and that incomplete applications are not considered for an award.
Exceeding the entitlement period without documented valid reasons under Sections 18 and 19 StudFG.
Applying for the funding scholarship after the thesis has already been completed or assessed.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition and fees remain entirely yours: third-country degree students pay EUR 726.72 per semester plus the OeH fee, EU/EEA students pay EUR 25.20 per semester during the tolerance period and EUR 363.36 after it, and no Graz scholarship waives those charges. Living costs, accommodation in Graz, insurance and travel between your home town and Graz are likewise unfunded.
document_audit: Non-Austrian applicants must upload proof of belonging to the eligible group of persons; a passport photo page by itself does not establish eligibility.

Anything missing from UNIGRAZonline must be attached manually - recognition notifications plus the underlying certificate where the recognition shows no grade, and transcripts for exams taken elsewhere.
SOWI requires the 'Beiblatt' supplementary sheet converted to PDF; without it the application cannot be processed at all, and the sheet must be filled on a computer.
For the funding scholarship you need a cost statement that also discloses every other funding source you have applied to and any amount already awarded, plus at least one expert opinion.
Keep original receipts: the funding scholarship pays 75% up front and the remaining 25% only after a report with an accounting form and original receipts is submitted on time.
alerts: The common catalogue-style claim of a tuition-fee waiver and a 'monthly stipend' is not supported anywhere on the university's own pages - treat it as incorrect until a faculty confirms otherwise.
Although the programme is marketed to 'international students', third-country nationals without equal status are excluded, which is the single biggest eligibility trap.
Decisions arrive by e-mail by the end of the calendar year, and faculties explicitly ask applicants not to call or write to chase the outcome.
An application is still possible if you finished your studies before the end of the academic year or are currently on leave of absence - do not assume graduation disqualifies you.
A funding-scholarship report submitted late forfeits the remaining 25%, and non-submission after a reminder can require full repayment of funds already received.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Open the 'Merit Scholarship' app in UNIGRAZonline between 21 September and 30 October, register bank details, upload the residence registration, passport and (for non-Austrians) equal-status proof, submit to the single faculty where you earned most ECTS, then wait for the dean's e-mail decision by year end.
